newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on govt officials' remarks.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on govt officials' remarks.

text.p: The key June three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures on TIFFE ended easier on Wednesday, in line with the tumble in yen bonds following remarks by government officials that recent rises in yen bond prices were not in line with the performance of the economy.
The June fell to a low of 99.18 just after the remarks, but recovered some ground on dealers' bargain-hunting bids, traders said.

"Looking at yen bond futures, the upward trend is still in place, though the excessive rally has somewhat subsided. There is a clear discrepancy between the economic reality and the trend in the yen bond market," one official told Reuters.
Another official said he saw no need for implementing a supplementary budget, judging from the recovery trend.

Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said late on Wednesday afternoon that Japan's economy is recovering gradually, with private consumption resuming a gradual recovery after being somewhat sluggish in the summer.
Matsushita also said that Japan's economic recovery seems to be becoming solid now.
Bullish comments from the government made some traders believe that the recent rally in the debt market across the yield curve may have been overdone, traders said.

However, others said that despite the market falls today, it is still difficult for traders to go decisively short after having suffered significant losses on short squeezing in the past several months.
The overnight call rate was most actively traded at 0.48-0.49 percent, up from 0.47 percent on Tuesday.
The key three month certificates of deposit (CDs) were at 0.51 percent, unchanged from Tuesday.
The Bank of Japan conducted a neutral operation this morning by injecting 600 billion yen into the money market where the projected shortfall was expected to be 610 billion yen.
Interest rates at the long end of the yield curve were also pushed up in reaction to dealers' speculative selling of yen bond futures and buying of Nikkei stock futures, traders said.
